title: Projective modules lift across a nilpotent quotient
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal with $I^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$. For every projective $A/I$-module $\overline P$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], there exist a projective $A$-module $P$ and an isomorphism $P/IP\cong\overline P$ of $A/I$-modules. No finite generation is assumed.

proof.text: By the direct-summand characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], choose a set $S$ and maps $i:\overline P\to\overline F=(A/I)^{(S)}$ and $s:\overline F\to\overline P$ with $si=1$. Put $\overline p=is$. Then $\overline p^2=\overline p$ and its image is $i(\overline P)$, identified with $\overline P$ by $s$. Set $F=A^{(S)}$.

source.place: Tag 07LV, lemma-lift-projective-module, first sentence; Tag 05CF, lemma-characterize-projective

proof.text: The coordinate reduction $q:F\to\overline F$ is surjective with kernel $IF$: every vector has finite support, its coefficients lift individually, and a vector with coefficients in $I$ is a finite sum of elements $a e_j$ with $a\in I$. For each basis vector $e_j$, lift the finitely supported vector $\overline p(q(e_j))$ to $v_j\in F$. Define $p(\sum_j a_j e_j)=\sum_j a_jv_j$. This is an $A$-linear endomorphism with $qp=\overline p q$. No bound on the cardinality of $S$ is used.

source.place: Tag 07LV, lemma-lift-projective-module, choice of a lift of the projector

proof.text: Write $x=p^2-p$. The equality $qx=0$ implies $x(F)\subseteq IF$. By $A$-linearity, $x(I^kF)\subseteq I^{k+1}F$ for every $k\geq0$, since applying $x$ to a finite sum $\sum a_j f_j$ gives $\sum a_jx(f_j)$. Induction gives $x^N(F)\subseteq I^NF=0$, so $x^N=0$ in the (possibly noncommutative) ring $\operatorname{End}_A(F)$.

source.place: Tag 07LV, lemma-lift-projective-module, nilpotence of the lifted projector defect

proof.text: Let $R=\mathbf Z[t]/((t^2-t)^N)$, write $u$ for the class of $t$, and let $J=(u^2-u)\subseteq R$. This is a commutative ring with $J^N=0$, and $u\bmod J$ is idempotent. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lift-idempotents-locally-nilpotent] to obtain an idempotent $v\in R$ with $v-u\in J$. All elements of $J$ are nilpotent because their $N$th powers lie in $J^N=0$.

source.place: Tag 05BU, lemma-lift-idempotents-noncommutative, proof using Tag 00J9, lemma-lift-idempotents

proof.text: Evaluation at $p$ defines a ring homomorphism $R\to\operatorname{End}_A(F)$: integer scalars commute with $p$, and the defining relation evaluates to $x^N=0$. Let $e$ be the image of $v$. Then $e^2=e$. Since $v-u\in J$, its image is a multiple of $x$ by a polynomial in $p$, hence sends $F$ into $IF$. Thus $qe=qp=\overline p q$. This is the polynomial correction of Tag 05BU, derived from the cited commutative lifting statement rather than assuming that the endomorphism ring is commutative.

source.place: Tag 05BU, lemma-lift-idempotents-noncommutative, evaluation of the universal polynomial lift; Tag 07LV

proof.text: Set $P=\operatorname{Im}(e)$. The inclusion $P\to F$ and the map $F\to P$, $f\mapsto e(f)$, compose to the identity on $P$, so [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] makes $P$ projective. The restriction of $q$ maps $P$ onto $\operatorname{Im}(\overline p)$: for $\overline p(\bar f)$ choose $f$ with $q(f)=\bar f$ and use $q(e(f))=\overline p(\bar f)$. Its kernel is $P\cap IF=IP$: one inclusion is immediate, and if $y\in P\cap IF$, write $y=\sum_j a_jf_j$ with $a_j\in I$; then $y=e(y)=\sum_j a_je(f_j)\in IP$. Hence $[y]\mapsto s(q(y))$ defines an $A/I$-linear bijection $P/IP\to\overline P$. Its inverse sends $z\in\overline P$ to $[e(f)]$ for any lift $f$ of $i(z)$; different lifts differ in $IF$, whose image under $e$ lies in $IP$. The first composition sends $z$ to $s(q(e(f)))=s(\overline p(i(z)))=si(z)=z$. For $y\in P$, choose $f=y$ as a lift of $i(s(q(y)))=\overline p(q(y))=q(y)$; the other composition sends $[y]$ to $[e(y)]=[y]$. Linearity of $s\circ q$ and the equality $I(P/IP)=0$ give the asserted $A/I$-linearity.

source.place: Tag 07LV, lemma-lift-projective-module, final image construction and verification of reduction
